assertions.text: Output contains at least 2 separate markdown tables
assertions.evidence: ## 1. Free Trial Eligibility ... ## 2. Subscription Price ... ## 3. Plan Switching ... ## 4a. Refund Eligibility ... ## 4b. Prorated Refund Amount

assertions.text: A table or note explicitly captures that the free trial is not available on annual plans (not just implied)
assertions.evidence: New subscriber picks annual | New | Annual | {yes, no} | no |

assertions.text: At least one table row demonstrates the loyalty programme discount scenario for annual plan subscribers
assertions.evidence: Annual plan, loyalty member | Annual | yes | 10% | £86.29

assertions.text: The response identifies at least one genuinely underspecified interaction — such as: what happens when a trial subscriber upgrades to annual mid-trial, when a subscriber joins the loyalty programme mid-billing-cycle, or whether a cancellation refund is based on the discounted or full price. These are NOT stated in the rules and require a product decision.
assertions.evidence: If a loyalty membership lapses mid-annual-cycle, does the discount hold for the rest of the paid term or only for future renewals?

assertions.text: The annual/loyalty/trial interaction is correctly resolved with a note explaining that they are mutually exclusive (annual gets loyalty discounts but no trial, monthly gets trial but no loyalty discount) — not left as an unresolved open question
assertions.evidence: Loyalty membership never affects Monthly pricing or trial eligibility — the discount rule only touches Annual.

assertions.text: Makes clear (via table structure, a note, or explicit rows) that the loyalty discount applies to the annual plan only — a loyalty member on monthly pays the same as anyone else.

The loyalty annual subscriber's prorated cancellation refund is either surfaced as an open question (discounted vs list price) OR calculated from the discounted price with a visible trace — since that is what was actually paid
Includes a cancellation/refund table or section (not just pricing) — the loyalty discount creates a refund calculation ambiguity that should be shown with concrete rows.
assertions.evidence: ## 4a. Refund Eligibility on Cancellation ... ## 4b. Prorated Refund Amount

assertions.text: The cancellation/refund table includes a loyalty member column (or equivalent) to distinguish loyalty vs non-loyalty annual refund rows — not just plan type alone.

The '?' suffix is only used on output or derived columns (e.g. 'Refund?', 'Price?') — not on given input columns like plan type, loyalty status, or subscription phase. A column that interprets or classifies an input value (e.g. deriving whether a cancellation falls within 24h from a raw time value) is a valid derived output and may use '?'.
assertions.evidence: Trial Granted? Trial Length? Price? Charged Immediately? Refund Given? Refund Amount?

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules. Acceptable to use a single table only when the domain genuinely has a single concern.
assertions.evidence: Four tables emerged as separate concerns: trial eligibility, pricing, plan switching..., and cancellation refunds.

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns. Fewer rows per table is expected when concerns are properly separated.
assertions.evidence: Each table (e.g. '1. Free Trial Eligibility' with 4 rows, '2. Subscription Price' with 3 rows) contains only rows needed for its own rule set.

assertions.text: Pricing/plans, trial eligibility, loyalty discount applicability, and cancellation/refund are in separate tables
assertions.evidence: Table '2. Subscription Price' merges pricing and loyalty discount applicability into one table rather than giving loyalty its own separate table.
